title: Quasi-coherent module descent along a general smooth atlas
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal X/S$ an algebraic stack [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and $a:U\to\mathcal X$ a smooth surjective scheme atlas. Let $R=U\times_{\mathcal X}U$ and $R_2=U\times_{\mathcal X}U\times_{\mathcal X}U$ be the $2$-fibre products of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], with projections $p_1,p_2:R\to U$, $p_{ij}:R_2\to R$ and diagonal $e:U\to R$. The relation spaces are algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] and need not be schemes. Use the big fppf ringed site of $\mathcal X$ [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra] and module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Quasi-coherent modules on that site and on algebraic spaces use the local-presentation predicate of [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Restriction to a scheme test uses [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction]. Tensor pullbacks on schemes and on small etale algebraic-space sites use [def-pc-module-pullback, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Restriction to $U$ gives an equivalence from $\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal X)$ to the category of pairs $(M,\delta)$, where $M$ is a quasi-coherent module on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], $\delta:p_1^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}p_2^*M$, $e^*\delta=1$, and $p_{23}^*\delta\circ p_{12}^*\delta=p_{13}^*\delta$ on $R_2$, with canonical pullback identifications understood. The functor sends $F$ to $(F_U,\delta_F)$, where $F_U$ is the restriction of $F$ to $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $\delta_F=(c_2^F)^{-1}c_1^F$, with $c_i^F:p_i^*F_U\xrightarrow{\sim}F_R$ the comparison isomorphisms of [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction] into the restriction $F_R$ of $F$ along the canonical object of $\mathcal X$ over $R$, interpreted on etale scheme charts; it sends a module map to its restriction to $U_{\mathrm{et}}$. Morphisms $(M,\delta_M)\to(N,\delta_N)$ are all module maps $b:M\to N$ such that $\delta_N\circ p_1^*b=p_2^*b\circ\delta_M$. In particular every such pair descends to a quasi-coherent big-fppf module with a specified isomorphism on $U$ respecting the datum, and compatible maps descend uniquely. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, Noetherian, finiteness or Deligne--Mumford hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06WT, proposition-quasi-coherent, applied to the smooth presentation of Tag 04T5 (algebraic.tex, lemma-stack-presentation); stacks-sheaves.tex section-quasi-coherent-algebraic-stacks.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], the representable smooth atlas $a$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Its surjectivity is part of the hypothesis. Apply clause (2) of [lem-sfb-fppf-groupoid-stack-presentations] to $a$. It supplies the self-relation groupoid $(U,R,s=p_1,t=p_2,e,i,c)$ and the canonical equivalence $K:[U/R]\to\mathcal X$ commuting with $a$. Here an arrow $r:u\to v$ is an isomorphism $a(u)\to a(v)$; composition is composition of these isomorphisms. The relation remains an algebraic space: no scheme presentation for $R$ is assumed.

Compare the datum category in the statement with the groupoid-module category defined in [lem-sfb-space-groupoid-module-descent]. Send $(M,\delta)$ to $(M,\alpha=\delta^{-1})$, and leave module maps unchanged. Identify a triple $(u_1,u_2,u_3)$ with the composable pair $(r_{23},r_{12})$. Then $\delta_{13}=\delta_{23}\delta_{12}$ is equivalent, on taking inverses, to $\alpha_{13}=\alpha_{12}\alpha_{23}$, exactly that node's composition rule. The identity rules agree. Multiplying $\delta_Np_1^*b=p_2^*b\delta_M$ by the inverse data gives $p_1^*b\alpha_M=\alpha_Np_2^*b$, its morphism rule. Taking inverses again is the inverse functor. Thus these categories are isomorphic, including all their morphisms.

The equivalence $K$ of step 1 identifies quasi-coherent big-fppf modules on $\mathcal X$ and on $[U/R]$. Explicitly choose an inverse $L$ over the base and the unit and counit. Precomposition with $K$ and $L$ preserves sheaves: objects, arrows and covering families correspond, since both functors preserve the underlying schemes and covers are precisely fppf covers of those schemes. They preserve the structure rings $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. A local presentation by sums of these rings therefore remains a local presentation. Applying a module sheaf to the unit and counit gives inverse natural isomorphisms between the two composites and the identity. This proves the claimed equivalence on the full quasi-coherent subcategories, as well as on all module maps.

source.place: Tag 06WT, reduction to a quotient presentation; elementary precomposition along an equivalence of fibred categories.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-groupoid-module-descent] to the algebraic-space groupoid of step 1: its object space is the scheme $U$ regarded as an algebraic space by [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space], its arrow space is $R$, and $[U/R]$ is its fppf stackification. That theorem gives an equivalence from quasi-coherent big-fppf modules on $[U/R]$ to its groupoid modules. Compose it with step 3 and the inverse of step 2. This is the functor asserted here, not merely an unspecified equivalence: the specified $Kx\simeq a$ identifies the object module with $F_U$, and identifies the groupoid two-arrow with the canonical isomorphism between the two objects over $R$. By [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction], the comparisons $c_i^F$ are tensor-pullback isomorphisms, natural in $F$ and compatible with composition. Contravariance along the arrow $a(u_1)\to a(u_2)$ makes the groupoid datum $(c_1^F)^{-1}c_2^F:p_2^*F_U\to p_1^*F_U$. Step 2 inverts this to $(c_2^F)^{-1}c_1^F=\delta_F$. These computations are on etale scheme charts of $R$ and $R_2$, exactly the interpretation in the statement. On a module map each functor takes its restriction to $U$, so the composite has the specified action on morphisms.

source.place: Tag 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent), first construction of the restriction functor; Tag 06WK (lemma-quasi-coherent), pullback comparisons.

proof.text: For any prescribed $(M,\delta)$, essential surjectivity of the equivalence just proved supplies $F$ and an isomorphism from its image to $(M,\delta)$. By the displayed morphism rule this is precisely an isomorphism $F_U\simeq M$ respecting the datum. Full faithfulness says that every compatible module map is the restriction of exactly one map on $\mathcal X$. These are the final two assertions. Every use above allows arbitrary algebraic spaces and the original smooth surjective atlas; no quasi-compactness, separatedness, Noetherian, finite-generation or Deligne--Mumford hypothesis was added.

Step 1: chartwise calculus gives smooth ⇒ flat and lfp, and clause (2) of fppf-groupoid-stack-presentations then gives the self-relation groupoid and the equivalence [U/R] ≃ X commuting with a. Step 2: I checked the orientation by hand. With s=p1, t=p2 and α=δ^{-1}, the composable pair (r23,r12) turns α13=α12α23 into δ13=δ23δ12, and the morphism rule s^*v∘α=β∘t^*v matches the item's. Step 4: Kx≅a and the 2-arrow x∘s⇒x∘t turn 06WT's α_F into (c1)^{-1}c2, whose inverse is the stated δ_F; module maps go to their restrictions, and R and R2 are handled on étale charts only. Step 5 is elementary. Edge cases: the identity atlas, the empty stack, BG with G positive-dimensional (so no DM property is used), and infinite unions; the δ direction also agrees with the citer coherator-flat-test-restriction. Every cited statement is in unit sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability and no tool_uses are needed.
